newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan body rejects claims of army vote-rigging.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan body rejects claims of army vote-rigging.

text.p: Pakistans official Election Commission on Saturday rejected claims that the army had joined alleged rigging of general elections on February 3 to defeat ousted prime minister Benazir Bhuttos Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP).

The allegation was made by many defeated PPP candidates at a meeting with Bhutto on Thursday as they discussed the partys crushing defeat in the elections, which gave a landslide victory to the Pakistan Muslim League party of former prime minister Nawaz Sharif.

An Election Commission meeting on Saturday took a "strong exception to the uncalled criticism against the Pakistan army" and called the charges unfortunate, a Commission statement quoted by the official APP news agency said.

"It is unfortunate that some of the leaders, in order to further their selfish aims, sometimes issue such statements which are far beyond the realm of realities and are against the national interest," said the Commission statement quoted by the official APP news agency.

Speakers at Thursdays PPP meeting had accused troops of virtually controlling polling stations, coaxing voters to vote against the PPP, stamping ballot papers and taking civilian officers who presided over the voting into custody.
Bhutto has refused to accept the election result but said she would not launch a protest for the sake of Pakistans stability.

The Election Commission expressed its satisfaction at overall arrangements made for the elections and "lauded the role of armed forces in maintaining law and order" on polling day, the Commission statement said.

It said the army had been deployed to help the election authorities in response to demands from a number of political parties and independent candidates "so that the voters could cast their votes without any fear and intimidation".

The Election Commission had "thought it in the best public interest to call for the assistance of the armed forces...so that the norms of democracy in the country could be strengthened by holding free, fair and transparent general elections in accordance with the provisions of the law", it said.
